summary.goal: Implement a SessionAdapter that reads from the agent-relay daemon's actual storage. Unlike the generic relay-JSONL adapter (which reads plain JSONL files), this adapter understands the daemon's SQLite message store and its JSONL archive format with Envelope<T> wrappers, SendPayload/ChannelMessagePayload types, and agent lifecycle events. It can also read from the daemon's SQLite database directly for more structured access. Sessions are reconstructed from continuous message streams by agent lifecycle boundaries (spawn -> release) or time windows.

acceptance_criteria.description: Reads from .agent-relay/messages/ directory (JSONL archives) with proper Envelope<T> parsing
Optionally reads from .agent-relay/ daemon SQLite for structured message access
SendPayload (DM) messages -> Message with agentName = from field, role = agent
ChannelMessagePayload messages -> Message with channel context in metadata
Broadcast messages (TO: *) -> Message with role = system
Agent spawn events -> SessionEvent with type agent_spawned
Agent release events -> SessionEvent marking session boundary

Session reconstruction uses three strategies in priority order: 1) channel-based (messages in #plan-{uuid} = one session), 2) agent lifecycle (spawn -> release = one session), 3) time-gap fallback (30 min configurable gap = session boundary)
Fallback session grouping: when no clear lifecycle events, group by time window (configurable, default 30 min gap)
agentFilter config: limit to messages from/to specific agents
channelFilter config: limit to specific channels (e.g., #plan-{uuid})
Cross-project bridge messages tagged with project context in metadata
getCursor/setCursor track by agent name or channel
Config: { dataDir: string, mode: 'jsonl' | 'sqlite', agentFilter?: string[], channelFilter?: string[], sessionGapMinutes?: number }
Defines minimal local types for JSONL parsing (RelayEnvelope, RelaySendPayload, RelayChannelPayload) — does NOT import from relay SDK to keep mull portable
Channel-based session reconstruction: all messages in #plan-{uuid} grouped as one session with id = plan-{uuid}

observations: This differs from the generic relay-JSONL adapter: it understands the daemon's specific message types (SendPayload, ChannelMessagePayload, Envelope<T>)
Session boundary detection is the key challenge: relay messages are a continuous stream, not session-delimited
Agent spawn -> release lifecycle provides natural session boundaries for agent-to-agent work
Channel-based grouping: #plan-{uuid} channels naturally scope to a planning session
JSONL files are date-partitioned (YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl) — need to read across date boundaries for multi-day sessions
SQLite mode provides structured queries (WHERE from_name = ? AND timestamp > ?) vs. scanning JSONL
This adapter is plannr-specific because it depends on relay daemon storage format — the generic JSONL adapter handles simple formats
Local type definitions for relay wire format keep mull portable — no runtime dependency on the relay SDK package
concerns: Relay daemon SQLite schema is not documented in this monorepo — need to inspect .agent-relay/ files or read relay source
Session reconstruction heuristics: time-gap-based grouping may split sessions that had a long pause
Large JSONL archives: scanning all messages for agent filtering could be slow without indexing

steps.title: Define minimal local types for relay wire format

acceptance_criteria.description: Local types defined in relay-types.ts, no imports from relay SDK
RelayEnvelope<T> covers id, type, timestamp, payload
Payload types cover SendPayload, ChannelPayload, SpawnPayload, ReleasePayload
Types are minimal — only fields needed for mull extraction

steps.specification: The relay SDK (agent-relay package) defines Envelope, SendPayload, ChannelMessagePayload etc. We intentionally do NOT import these because: 1) mull should be portable across relay versions, 2) we only need a subset of fields, 3) if relay types change, mull's defensive parsing handles it gracefully rather than a compile-time break.

steps.title: Create RelayDaemonAdapter class with dual-mode connection
steps.description: Create packages/mull/src/adapters/relay-daemon-adapter.ts. Implement class RelayDaemonAdapter that implements SessionAdapter. Constructor accepts config: { dataDir: string, mode: 'jsonl' | 'sqlite', agentFilter?: string[], channelFilter?: string[], sessionGapMinutes?: number }. In 'sqlite' mode, open the daemon's SQLite DB with better-sqlite3({ readonly: true }). In 'jsonl' mode, store the messages directory path for lazy file reading. Default sessionGapMinutes to 30.

acceptance_criteria.description: RelayDaemonAdapter implements SessionAdapter
Supports 'jsonl' and 'sqlite' modes via config
SQLite mode opens DB with { readonly: true }
sessionGapMinutes defaults to 30

steps.specification: Location: packages/mull/src/adapters/relay-daemon-adapter.ts. Config type: RelayDaemonAdapterConfig = { dataDir: string, mode: 'jsonl' | 'sqlite', agentFilter?: string[], channelFilter?: string[], sessionGapMinutes?: number }. Constructor: if mode==='sqlite', open DB at {dataDir}/relay.db with better-sqlite3({ readonly: true }). If mode==='jsonl', store messagesDir = path.join(dataDir, 'messages'). Note: JSONL is the primary mode based on actual relay daemon behavior — SQLite is secondary.

steps.title: Implement JSONL reader with date-partitioned file handling
steps.description: Implement a JSONL reader module at packages/mull/src/adapters/relay-jsonl-reader.ts. Reads .agent-relay/messages/ directory which contains date-partitioned JSONL files (YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl). The reader: 1) Lists all JSONL files in the directory sorted by date, 2) For a given time range (after/before), only opens relevant date-partitioned files, 3) Reads each file line-by-line, 4) Parses each line as RelayEnvelope<unknown>, 5) Detects envelope type and parses payload as the appropriate RelaySendPayload/RelayChannelPayload/etc, 6) Applies agentFilter (from/to fields) and channelFilter, 7) Returns filtered RelayEnvelope[] array. Defensive parsing — malformed lines are skipped with a warning, not a crash.

acceptance_criteria.description: Reads date-partitioned JSONL files from .agent-relay/messages/
Only opens JSONL files within the requested time range
Parses each line as RelayEnvelope, detects type, parses payload
Applies agentFilter and channelFilter during read
Malformed lines skipped with warning, not crash

steps.specification: Location: packages/mull/src/adapters/relay-jsonl-reader.ts. Export readRelayJsonl(messagesDir: string, opts?: { after?: string, before?: string, agentFilter?: string[], channelFilter?: string[] }): RelayEnvelope[]. Date filtering: parse YYYY-MM-DD from filenames, compare with opts.after/before dates to skip irrelevant files. Line parsing: for each line, JSON.parse wrapped in try/catch. Type detection: envelope.type determines payload parser. Agent filter: check payload.from and payload.to fields. Channel filter: check payload.channel field.

steps.title: Implement session reconstruction algorithm
steps.description:
Implement session reconstruction in packages/mull/src/adapters/relay-session-reconstructor.ts. Takes a stream of RelayEnvelope[] (already filtered) and groups them into sessions. Uses three strategies in priority order:

1) Channel-based: Messages in #plan-{uuid} channels are grouped by channel. Session ID = the channel name (e.g., 'plan-abc123'). All messages in the same channel belong to one session regardless of timing.

2) Agent lifecycle: For non-channel messages, look for spawn/release envelope pairs. Messages between a spawn and its corresponding release (matched by agent name) form one session. Session ID = '{agent_name}-{spawn_timestamp}'.

3) Time-gap fallback: For remaining ungrouped messages, sort by timestamp and split into sessions wherever the gap between consecutive messages exceeds sessionGapMinutes (default 30). Session ID = 'gap-{first_message_timestamp}'.

Return Map<sessionId, RelayEnvelope[]> where each value is the chronologically ordered messages for that session.

acceptance_criteria.description: Channel-based grouping: #plan-{uuid} messages grouped by channel name
Agent lifecycle grouping: spawn->release pairs define session boundaries
Time-gap fallback: messages split by configurable gap (default 30 min)
Strategies applied in priority order: channel > lifecycle > time-gap
Returns Map<sessionId, RelayEnvelope[]> with chronological ordering
Messages that match channel strategy are NOT re-processed by lifecycle or time-gap strategies

steps.specification: The three strategies are applied as a waterfall: channel-based claims messages first, then lifecycle claims from the remainder, then time-gap handles whatever is left. A message belongs to exactly one session. Channel-based is highest priority because #plan-{uuid} channels provide the strongest semantic grouping.

steps.title: Implement listSessions and getSession using reconstruction
steps.description: Wire up the adapter's SessionAdapter methods. listSessions: 1) In JSONL mode, use the JSONL reader to load all envelopes within the time range, then run session reconstruction, return SessionRef[] with id, firstEvent, lastEvent, messageCount. 2) In SQLite mode, query the daemon's message table with filters, reconstruct sessions from results. getSession(sessionId): Load the specific session's envelopes and map to SessionData. Mapping rules: SendPayload -> Message(agentName=from, role='agent', content=body), ChannelMessagePayload -> Message(agentName=from, role='agent', content=body, metadata.channel), Broadcast (to='*') -> Message(role='system'), SpawnPayload -> SessionEvent(type='agent_spawned', agentName=name), ReleasePayload -> SessionEvent(type='session_boundary').

acceptance_criteria.description: listSessions works in both JSONL and SQLite modes
getSession maps SendPayload to Message with agentName and role='agent'
getSession maps ChannelMessagePayload to Message with channel in metadata
getSession maps broadcast messages to Message with role='system'
Spawn/release envelopes mapped to SessionEvent types
Cross-project bridge messages include project context in metadata

steps.specification: Location: methods on RelayDaemonAdapter class. listSessions: load all envelopes via JSONL reader (or SQLite query), run session reconstruction, return SessionRef[] per reconstructed session. getSession: load specific session's envelopes from reconstruction cache or re-reconstruct. Message mapping: switch on envelope.type — 'message' with to='*' -> role='system', 'message' with named to -> role='agent', 'channel_message' -> role='agent' with metadata.channel. Bridge messages detected by 'project:' prefix in from/to fields.

steps.title: Implement cursor tracking by agent name or channel
steps.description: Implement getCursor/setCursor that track progress per agent name or channel. Cursor files stored at .mull/cursors/relay/{identifier}.json where identifier is the agent name or channel name. For channel-based sessions, the cursor tracks by channel. For agent lifecycle sessions, by agent name. For time-gap sessions, by a synthetic key. Cursor contains { lastTimestamp, lastProcessedAt, messageCount }.

acceptance_criteria.description: Cursors stored in .mull/cursors/relay/{identifier}.json
Channel sessions tracked by channel name
Agent lifecycle sessions tracked by agent name
Cursor includes lastTimestamp, lastProcessedAt, messageCount

steps.title: Write tests for JSONL parsing, session reconstruction, and mapping
steps.description:
Create packages/mull/src/adapters/__tests__/relay-daemon-adapter.test.ts. Tests:
- JSONL reader: parse valid envelopes, skip malformed lines, date-partitioned file selection
- Session reconstruction: channel-based grouping, spawn->release lifecycle grouping, time-gap fallback, priority ordering (channel > lifecycle > time-gap)
- Message mapping: SendPayload -> Message, ChannelPayload -> Message with channel metadata, Broadcast -> system role, Spawn/Release -> SessionEvents
- Agent and channel filters applied correctly
- Cursor tracking: save/load cursor, incremental processing
- Edge cases: empty JSONL files, single-message sessions, multi-day sessions spanning date boundaries

Create temp directories with test JSONL files for JSONL mode tests. Use Vitest.

acceptance_criteria.description: Tests cover JSONL parsing with valid and malformed input
Tests cover all three session reconstruction strategies and their priority order
Tests cover message type mapping (DM, channel, broadcast, spawn, release)
Tests cover agent and channel filtering
Tests cover cursor tracking and incremental processing
All tests pass with Vitest

criteria.note: Only JSONL mode implemented, no SQLite mode
Channel messages detected but no metadata field added
Broadcasts detected but not mapped to role=system
Session boundaries from sessions.jsonl, not release events
Lifecycle grouping only, no channel or time-gap strategies
No time-gap fallback or sessionGapMinutes config
No project context / bridge message handling
Config only has dataDir and sessionsFile, missing mode/filters
